title: Multi-file in-memory contacts package (layered: model, repo, service, serializer)
prompt:
Build a small, layered, in-memory contacts management package in Python. It is deliberately spread across several files to mirror a real layered application. No database, no web server, no external dependencies (standard library only). Every file below MUST exist and the layers MUST be wired together.

## Required files (exact paths)

1. `contacts/__init__.py` -- marks the package. May re-export the public classes.

2. `contacts/validators.py` -- define:
       def is_valid_email(email) -> bool
   Returns True for a plausibly valid email (has a local part, an `@`, and a
   domain with a dot), False otherwise. `is_valid_email("a@b.com")` is True;
   `is_valid_email("not-an-email")` and `is_valid_email("")` are False.

3. `contacts/models.py` -- define a `Contact` class constructed as
   `Contact(name=..., email=...)` with at least `name` and `email` attributes,
   and an optional `id` attribute (default None until stored).

4. `contacts/repository.py` -- define `ContactRepository`, an in-memory store:
       - `add(contact) -> Contact`  assigns a unique integer `id` (start at 1)
         and stores it; returns the stored contact.
       - `get(contact_id) -> Contact`  returns the stored contact or None.
       - `list() -> list`  returns all stored contacts.

5. `contacts/service.py` -- define `ContactService(repository)` (constructor
   takes a repository instance) with:
       - `add_contact(name, email) -> Contact`  VALIDATES the email using
         `is_valid_email`; if invalid it RAISES a `ValueError`. Otherwise it
         builds a `Contact` and stores it via the repository, returning the
         stored contact (with its assigned `id`).
       - `get_contact(contact_id) -> Contact`
       - `list_contacts() -> list`

6. `contacts/serializers.py` -- define:
       def contact_to_dict(contact) -> dict
   Returns a plain dict with at least `name` and `email` keys (include `id` too).

## Wiring requirement
The service must use the repository for storage and the validator for email
checks. A full round trip must work: create a service over a fresh repository,
`add_contact("Grace Hopper", "grace@navy.mil")` returns a contact with an `id`,
`get_contact(id)` returns it back, `list_contacts()` includes it, and
`add_contact("Bad", "nope")` raises because the email is invalid.

Keep the code clean and split across the files exactly as listed above.
